clinical_category: Spirometry infection prevention - patient-contact mouthpiece and filter changes
blueprint_topic: Prevention of cross-contamination during shared pulmonary-function testing
stem: A nurse assists with spirometry testing for several clients using the same spirometer. Which infection-prevention action is appropriate between clients?

options.A: Change the spirometer mouthpiece and filter before the next client uses the equipment
options.B: Keep the same mouthpiece in place if it appears visibly clean
options.C: Replace the mouthpiece only at the end of the testing day
options.D: Reuse the same mouthpiece after wiping only its outside surface

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC disinfection guidance notes that mouthpieces and spirometry tubing can become contaminated with microorganisms and that, when filters are used to protect equipment distal to the filter, the filter and proximal mouthpiece are changed between patients. CDC's pneumonia-prevention guidance likewise directs changing the mouthpiece and filter of a spirometer between different patients. B, C, and D permit reuse of a patient-contact mouthpiece between clients and conflict with this infection-control practice.
educational_objective: Prevent cross-contamination during shared spirometry by changing the patient-contact mouthpiece and filter between clients.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: A Rational Approach to Disinfection and Sterilization; Guidelines for Preventing Health-Care-Associated Pneumonia
source_version_date: CDC Infection Control guidance current and accessed 2026-08-18; pulmonary-function equipment recommendation retained on current CDC web resources
source_locator: CDC 'A Rational Approach to Disinfection and Sterilization' → pulmonary-function equipment discussion: mouthpieces and spirometry tubing can become contaminated; filters may prevent distal equipment contamination; filters and proximal mouthpieces are changed between patients. CDC 'Guidelines for Preventing Health-Care-Associated Pneumonia' → Pulmonary-function testing equipment, recommendation 9.b: change the mouthpiece and filter of a spirometer between uses on different patients.
source_claim_supported: CDC guidance directly supports changing the spirometry mouthpiece and filter between patients to prevent reuse of contaminated patient-contact components.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control client-needs subcategory (10–16% of items), within Safe and Effective Care Environment; includes prevention of infection and safe handling of client-care equipment.
correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The source cited only a generic AARC homepage and combined disposable-component use with unspecified reusable-component disinfection. The final item uses current CDC infection-control guidance and tests the exact, directly supported action of changing the spirometry mouthpiece and filter between clients.
audit_findings: The generic AARC root URL failed the exact-locator requirement.
CDC directly identifies contamination of spirometry mouthpieces/tubing and the practice of changing the proximal mouthpiece and filter between patients.
The item was narrowed to the exact supported infection-control action rather than asserting a particular disinfection method for all reusable spirometry components.
All distractors involve inappropriate between-client reuse of the patient-contact mouthpiece and are not defensible.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no cueing, no unsupported cleaning interval, no second answer, and no unresolved conflict.
